qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Algorithms, phase three. Optimisation. This is how factories and AI find the best plan.
A factory chooses x units of product X, and y units of product Y.
Choose x of product X and y of product Y.
Each rule cuts the plane in half. The forbidden half turns red.
Each rule cuts the plane in half.
The overlap of the allowed halves is the feasible region.
The overlap is the feasible region.
Now we plug a plan into every rule. If it passes them all, it is legal.
Plug a plan into every rule. Pass all: legal.
Break even one rule and the plan is not allowed. Three of the five plans fail.
Break even one rule and it is not allowed.
Each plan earns a score, z equals three x plus two y.
Each plan earns a score: z = 3x + 2y.
Every point on this line scores the same.
Every point on this line scores the same.
Now slide the profit line outwards, until it leaves the region.
Slide the profit line outwards until it leaves.
It leaves at a corner, so we only need to check the corners.
It leaves at a corner, so check only the corners.
Start at a corner, and ask which direction gains the most.
Start at a corner. Which direction gains most?
Then walk until the nearest rule blocks the way. That brings us to the corner five, zero.
Walk until the nearest rule blocks the way.
Repeat. The letter s is what a rule has left over.
Repeat. s = what a rule has left over.
Leftovers cost profit, so now only y gains. The walk goes on along the material line.
Leftovers cost profit, so only y gains.
At the corner four, three, no direction gains. So it is optimal.
No direction gains: the corner is optimal.
A new problem has just one number. We want its lowest point.
New problem: one number. Find the lowest point.
If the curve falls and then rises, a minimum is trapped in between.
Falling, then rising: a minimum is trapped.
Bisection tests the middle, and asks whether the curve is still falling.
Bisection: test the middle. Still falling?
Then we keep the half where the slope flips.
Keep the half where the slope flips.
Each step halves the bracket, and the minimum stays trapped inside.
Each step halves the bracket.
Golden section needs no slope. Three heights trap the minimum.
Golden section: no slope, three heights trap it.
Each step adds one probe, and the lowest point stays in the middle.
One probe a step: the lowest stays in the middle.
Old probes are reused, so each cut costs just one new test.
Old probes are reused, so each cut costs one test.
Each step keeps zero point six one eight of the bracket. This is the golden section.
Each step keeps 0.618 of the bracket.
On the same curve, fit a parabola through three points.
Same curve: fit a parabola through three points.
Then jump straight to the bottom of the parabola.
Jump to the bottom of the parabola.
Repeat, and the bracket collapses fast.
Repeat: the bracket collapses fast.
If the jump is not shrinking enough, take a golden step instead.
Jump not shrinking? Take a golden step instead.
With the same seven tests, the bracket is five times tighter.
Same 7 tests, a bracket 5 times tighter.
With two numbers and no slopes, we keep a triangle.
Two numbers, no slopes: keep a triangle.
Flip the worst corner through the middle of the best side.
Flip the worst corner through the middle.
If the flip is great, stretch even further.
A great flip? Stretch even further.
If the stretch goes too far, keep the plain flip.
Stretched too far? Keep the plain flip.
If the flip overshoots, pull the corner in instead.
Flip overshoots? Pull the corner in instead.
If every try fails, shrink the triangle towards the best corner.
If every try fails: shrink towards the best.
Real problems have curved valleys, not neat bowls.
Real problems have curved valleys, not bowls.
While the moves work, the triangle stretches.
Moves work? The triangle stretches.
With more good moves, it stretches along the valley.
More good moves: it stretches along the valley.
Near the end, it squeezes into a tiny triangle.
Near the end it squeezes to a tiny triangle.
No derivatives needed, just comparisons. Here it took eighty-four rounds.
No derivatives needed, just comparisons.
The best plan is at a corner, and simplex walks there.
Trap the minimum, then shrink the trap.
With no slope available, flip the worst corner.
